## 🔑 Core Claims of the Tretter Chronology
- The academic consensus on Ancient Near Eastern chronology is off by ~57 years
- A 48-week lunar calendar underlies biblical timekeeping (Sabbaths on 8th/15th/22nd/29th; new moons excluded from weekly count)
- 24 priestly courses rotate on a deterministic 24-year cycle anchored to 70 AD
- Hezekiah's sign (2 Kings 20:8-11) corresponds to the solar eclipse of April 15, 657 BC (Julian)
- A 120-Jubilee master cycle (5,880 years) spans Creation to 2040 AD
- VAT 4956 and Ptolemy's anchor eclipses support revised dates (512 BC / 666 BC) over conventional 586/721 BC
- The framework provides mathematical, statistical, and Bayesian validation of biblical chronology
